ledger_offload_funds_subchannel (ArmadaLean/Nitro/Liveness.lean) is FALSE as
currently stated (pebble aln-147's worker found this while attempting to
remove its sorry; left sorry in place per Lean proof doctrine, since the
statement cannot be proved and must not be weakened by a worker).

Counterexample (machine-checked, compiles with `lake env lean
docs/counterexamples/ledger_offload_funds_subchannel.lean`, exit 0):
docs/counterexamples/ledger_offload_funds_subchannel.lean

Argument: the theorem's hypotheses never require w.chi (the funded
sub-channel) to be a ledger channel. Adjudicator.transfer pays a destination
only when Address.fundable, which is true for a channel destination only
when its kind = .ledger (a virtual channel "holds no assets of its own and
is never credited this way", Address.lean:110-116).
Reachable.balances_virtual_zero then forces a virtual-kind channel's
on-chain balance to 0 at every reachable Adjudicator. So if w.chi.kind =
.virtual and w.c > 0, FundedFor apps (Ts.T w.A) w.chi w.c (v w.A) can never
be won by any honest strategy: no finite UnbeatableIn derivation exists
(not_unbeatable_of_virtual in the counterexample file, by induction on the
putative derivation).

The hypothesis w.Holds apps Ts v places no constraint on w.chi.kind at all:
it only requires w.L to be a ledger channel, finalizable (not yet landed)
with the three-way outcome [dA, dB, chi]. Finalizable/ConclusionProof check
only that the outcome is signed by every participant, never that its
destinations are later payable. So the hypothesis is exactly as satisfiable
for a virtual chi as for a ledger one: the counterexample file adapts
NonVacuity.lean's own funded witness for this theorem (wLSF/nLWF, "D10
ruling") verbatim, changing only chi's kind from .ledger to .virtual, and it
still satisfies every hypothesis, with w.c = 5 > 0.

docs/nitro-repair-2026-10-27.md (defect 23) already flagged this exact gap:
"Needs the G16 hypotheses of ledger_partial_withdrawal for chi" --
ledger_partial_withdrawal requires its receiving ledger L' to carry
IsLedgerChannel apps L' (Liveness.lean:7547); ledger_offload_funds_subchannel
never gained the analogous hypothesis for chi. Its re-audit row has been
updated from "unknown" to "false" with this counterexample cited.

Fix (requires an operator/coordinator statement-change decision, out of
scope for a sorry-removal worker): add a hypothesis
`(hchi : IsLedgerChannel apps w.chi)` to ledger_offload_funds_subchannel,
then re-attempt the proof (the witness machinery in
docs/counterexamples/ledger_offload_funds_subchannel.lean -- reachability
threading over Threat.RoundSeq, non-vacuity construction reuse -- is
directly reusable for the positive proof once chi is forced ledger-kind:
Address.fundable w.chi.address = true follows from hchi, letting
Adjudicator.transfer land L -> chi the same way ledger_partial_withdrawal's
conclude_transfer_pays lands L -> L').

Blocks aln-147 (cannot remove sorry from a false theorem without either
weakening/changing its statement, which a worker must not do unilaterally,
or using an unsound proof).

criticality: negligible

goal: Make sure a linting tool used to check Lean proofs stops incorrectly flagging a specific group of related declarations as duplicating the same hypothesis, without changing any of the underlying mathematical statements or breaking any other checks.

restatement:
  The Lean linter scripts/type_lint.lean currently emits a false-positive 'repeatedPremise' group for the premise `apps c.appDef = ArmadaLean.Nitro.consensusRules`, grouping together over twenty unrelated declarations in ArmadaLean.Nitro and ArmadaLean.Nitro.NonVacuity as if they repeat a hypothesis, when in fact the declarations treat it as one refined type or structure. The fix must make the linter stop reporting this group for this premise shape, without changing the meaning of any spec statement, and must preserve all existing gate invariants: scripts/check.sh --json must still report signatures_ok true and keep every _ok field true against scripts/gate-baseline.json (a full run may take up to 1500 seconds), the baseline must only be rewritten via scripts/update_gate_baseline.py when a count falls (never to raise a count without a fix), and a bare `lake clean` must never be run during the fix or verification.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: After the fix, running `lake build ArmadaLean ArmadaLean.Lint.TypeDoctrine` and `lake env lean scripts/type_lint.lean` must no longer print a repeatedPremise group whose premise is `apps c.appDef = ArmadaLean.Nitro.consensusRules` for the listed declarations.
- c2: No spec statement's meaning changes as part of this fix.
- c3: scripts/check.sh --json must report signatures_ok true after the fix.
- c4: scripts/check.sh --json must keep every _ok field true against scripts/gate-baseline.json, with a full run taking up to 1500 seconds.
- c5: If a count falls as a result of this fix, scripts/update_gate_baseline.py must be used to rewrite the baseline in the same branch (never used to raise a count or add a finding without a fix).
- c6: A bare `lake clean` must never be run in the course of implementing or verifying this fix.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: After building the project and running the type-lint script, the lint output should no longer contain a repeated-premise warning group about the premise 'apps c.appDef = ArmadaLean.Nitro.consensusRules' for the declarations that were fixed.
- c2: After the fix is applied, every statement in the spec file still means exactly what it meant before, except for the one statement the fix was allowed to change. A checker reads the spec, extracts each statement's identifier and wording, and confirms none of the untouched statements have been altered.
- c3: After the fix is applied, running the project's check script with the --json flag should show that signature checks passed, reported as signatures_ok: true in its output.
- c4: Running the repository's check script in JSON mode and comparing its output against the committed baseline file shows every '_ok' status flag reporting true, confirming nothing has regressed, and the whole check completes within 1500 seconds.
- c5: When a code fix causes a tracked issue count to go down, running the baseline update script should rewrite the baseline file to match the new, lower count — never to a higher one.
- c6: Check that the record of shell commands run while fixing and verifying this change never contains a plain, unqualified 'lake clean' invocation.

goal: Make a Lean definition called Pool.Call actually exist in the ArmadaLean project, shaped exactly as the documentation already describes it, while making sure nothing else in the proof project breaks or weakens.

restatement:
  In the ArmadaLean Lean 4 pool model, define a new constant Pool.Call as an inductive/structure with exactly the constructors required by Rule PE2: a shield constructor carrying the token, the gross amount and the note key; a transact constructor carrying the caller, the public inputs, the bound parameters, the proof, the optional unshield token, the disclosed records and the published openings; and an owned-transact constructor carrying the same fields as transact but with no unshield token. None of these constructors may carry a circuit witness (TransactWitness or TransactOwnedWitness). This must be achieved without changing any already-approved pool statement, without adding any new axiom, sorry, admit, native_decide, or #exit, without adding any file outside ArmadaLean/, without a bare lake clean, and without increasing any type-doctrine linter count above the gate baseline, while keeping scripts/check.sh --json fully passing.

- c1: Pool.Call exists as a declared constant, with #check @Pool.Call succeeding (no unknown-identifier error) when run via lake env lean on a file importing ArmadaLean.
- c2: Pool.Call has a shield constructor carrying exactly the token, the gross amount, and the note key.
- c3: Pool.Call has a transact constructor carrying exactly the caller, the public inputs, the bound parameters, the proof, the token of the unshield if there is one, the disclosed records, and the published openings.
- c4: Pool.Call has an owned-transact constructor carrying the same data as transact but with no unshield.
- c5: No constructor of Pool.Call carries a circuit witness (TransactWitness or TransactOwnedWitness).
- c6: scripts/check.sh --json reports signatures_ok true, showing no approved statement changed.
- c7: scripts/check.sh --json keeps every _ok field true against scripts/gate-baseline.json, and no type-doctrine linter count rises above the baseline.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: Anyone can check that the project defines a thing called Pool.Call by writing a tiny Lean file that imports the ArmadaLean library and asks Lean to check the type of Pool.Call. If Pool.Call is properly declared, Lean compiles the file without complaint and prints its type; if it isn't declared, Lean reports an 'unknown identifier' error.
- c2: Anyone can run a small check that builds a 'shield' call for the pool and see printed back exactly three pieces of information: the token, the gross amount, and the note key — nothing more and nothing less.
- c3: When someone creates a 'transact' call in the Pool system, the record they build should contain exactly seven pieces of information: the caller, the public inputs, the bound parameters, the proof, the optional unshield token, the disclosed records, and the published openings — nothing more, nothing less.
- c4: Anyone can check that the Pool.Call data type offers a special constructor for an 'owned transact' call, carrying all the same data fields as a normal transact call except for the unshield token, by searching the pool source code for this constructor and listing its field names.
- c5: Checking the source code of the Pool.Call type shows that none of its constructors include a circuit witness (TransactWitness or TransactOwnedWitness) as a field — calls only carry what a caller actually sends, not the private witness data.
